tema: extra inherits from another class; super calls the parent's constructor.

charla.texto: Junior, lesson two: inheritance. A class can inherit everything from another with extra, and then add its own stuff.
If the child class has its own constructor, it first has to call the parent's with super. Otherwise Coffee won't even let it exist.
It's the line of succession. The heir inherits the title, but first pays homage to the father.
inheritance: the one thing you'll never manage with your salary. the only thing they'll leave you is legacy code
If Rikka had a child class, would it inherit the butt? Because that would be quality legacy code.
Cami! The daughter would inherit my sword. And use it on you.
Exercise: an Intern that inherits from Employee. Earns the same as an Employee… minus everything.
codigo: // 1. Practicante inherits from Empleado with extra.

lineas: // Junior · Lesson 2: inheritance. Fill in the blanks.
// Expected output: Kevin has worked 40 hours (unpaid) / salary: decaf
pour cup.nombre + ' has worked ' + cup.horas + ' hours (unpaid)';
blend Child extra Parent { ... }  -> Child inherits everything from Parent (in other languages: extends).
super(...)                       -> calls the parent's constructor. It goes FIRST.
The Practicante class inherits trabajar() without writing it. That's the magic of inheritance: the work passes down on its own.

1.error: “{valor}” doesn't inherit. For Practicante to inherit from Empleado you write extra.

2.error: “{valor}” doesn't call the parent's constructor. Before using cup, you have to call super(nombre).

3.error: “{valor}” is too generous for an intern. The salary is nothing: decaf.

exito: Kevin has worked 40 hours (unpaid) / salary: decaf
✔ Compiled. The intern inherited everything from Empleado: the hours, the trabajar() method and the lack of pay.

Rikka: super first. The father always goes first, like at court.
